subject: qilin
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: qilin, scaled hooved chimera with antlers and cloud mane.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm sketching the qilin design: a deer-like body with a dragon head, antlers, scaled torso, cloud-like mane details, a fiery tail tuft, and cloven hooves, oriented as a quadruped facing forward with legs built using simple IK and the body sized proportionally along its length.

Now I'm working out the skeleton structure—placing hip, spine, neck, and head joints along a forward path, and building a separate tail chain branching backward from the hips with a downward-curving taper. I'm setting up the spine as a swept body shape with a radius function to give it form and taper.

Building the head geometry now: skull sphere, snout frustum, jaw joint, nostrils, whisker sweeps, and branching antlers via bezier curves off head.local points, plus leafy ear extrusions and a cloud-style card mane.

Now I'm scattering cloud-swirl texture cards along the neck sweep, filtering for upward-facing points, and adding extruded cloud plates along the back, then collecting frame positions for the cards. Moving on to legs, I'm setting up a loop over left/right sides to build front and hind limbs with shoulder joints, lengths, and bend parameters.

Adding cloven hooves as small dark-gold cylinder shapes at each leg tip, with sweep radius tapering down the leg, and planning flame-textured fetlock tufts near the ankles for a fiery accent.

I'm setting up scale-based paint with teal-jade on the back countershaded to a gold belly, applying the same material to the legs, then adding an ox-like tail with a flame tuft plus a gold decorative loop or saddle trim around the spine.

Adding more decoration...

Building out the snout, jaw joint, and fang spikes...

Now I'm skipping the tongue and placing eye decals by raycasting against the skull surface to find mirrored eye socket positions, then adding brow ridge spikes and sketching an antler horn path using catmull-rom curve points on each side.

Adding antler tines and spikes...

Now I'm figuring out ear geometry by extruding a leaf outline along the head bone, then setting up cloud-swirl texture cards for the mane—layering teal and white circles with outlines and placing them along the neck sweep at different angles.

I'm also scattering cloud puffs along the spine and legs to suggest the qilin walking on clouds, then deciding to skip hoof clouds in favor of flame tufts instead. For the flame details, I'm placing crossed cards at the tail tip and fetlocks, orienting them along the leg chain's tangent direction near the ankle.

Setting up small rings of flame cards around each leg tip with upward flow so the flames appear to rise naturally, confirming that the leg point chain correctly exposes a tip reference for positioning.

Now I'm working out hoof geometry as a cylinder with a darker cleft box to suggest a cloven hoof, and placing a gold swirl emblem decal on the shoulder using the body surface's normal direction for orientation.

For the gold accents, I'm sweeping a thin ring around the body near the hip joint using the spine's local frame for orientation. I'm also settling on a palette — jade green, dark teal, gold, cream, cloud teal, and flame orange — and planning a tapered jade tail sweep with flame-colored cards at the tip.

Now I'm working out the tail chain: four named points ending in a tip, a small ring of cards fanned at the end, and tuning their size, lean, and bend so they flow backward naturally. I'm also sketching out the hip offset and spine radius function to keep proportions consistent.

Then I'm building the neck as a chain attached to the spine's end, sweeping its radius down toward the head joint, and planning cheek and mane card details to finish the head region.
